clue.text: Salt one had put on bird's tail

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
the indefinite article an means one
had a meal, as in 'had lunch'

explanation.surface: Someone sprinkles salt on a bird's tail, the old joke about how to catch one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on bird's tail' says the second and third pieces are attached after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A titanate is a chemical salt formed from titanic acid, containing titanium and oxygen.

clue.text: Deficient, not finishing medical examination?

indicators.note: a word that does not finish has lost its final letter

blocks.note: scant means lacking or insufficient

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination that was cut short and so fell below standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan, such as an ultrasound or MRI, is a routine imaging check carried out by doctors.

clue.text: Children's book appeal embraced by fair-minded politicians

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be held inside someone else's arms

blocks.note: just means fair and impartial
an SOS is an urgent appeal for help
Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A plea to impartial politicians to support a book for young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The appeal is the Morse distress signal, which sits in the gap between the adjective and the party name.
explanation.definitionFit: Just So Stories is Rudyard Kipling's 1902 collection of fanciful origin tales written for young readers.

clue.text: See 3
Provide local gift

blocks.note: to do food or drinks is to provide them, as a café does lunches
a local is a native of the place

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply a gift sourced from the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a formal donation or bounty, especially money handed out by a ruler or patron.

clue.text: I'm strained - tricky to manage

indicators.note: something tricky is twisty and awkward, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stressed person complains that a task is hard to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer a business or estate is to run it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fish responsible for more than half the food poisoning

indicators.note: only a portion bigger than half of the following word is kept, and the remainder is dropped

blocks.note: salmonella is the bacterium behind much food poisoning

explanation.surface: A particular fish is blamed for most cases of food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the ten letters of SALMONELLA are kept, more than half, leaving SALMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon is a familiar pink-fleshed sea and river species prized for eating.

clue.text: Ignore incentive to buy?

blocks.note: first meaning: to disregard or dismiss as unimportant
second meaning: a price reduction offered to shoppers

explanation.surface: Advice to pay no attention to a sales promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means dismiss from consideration; as a noun it is a cut in price that tempts customers.

clue.text: Town actor who's been around a long time

blocks.clueFragment: who's been around a long time
blocks.note: someone who has been around for ages is old
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A town described as a veteran performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The description of the actor comes after him in the clue but goes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham is a large town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.

clue.text: Pressure to the north is building

blocks.note: the bar is a unit of atmospheric pressure
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A weather report: high pressure is building up over the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' places the second piece after the first. 'building' looks like a verb about pressure growing but is a noun for a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is a large farm structure for storing hay, grain or livestock.

clue.text: Land army hiding blunder if backed by military establishment

indicators.note: a thing doing the hiding keeps something else tucked inside it
backed means put into reverse, so the small word is read from end to start

blocks.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to err is to make a mistake
taken as written
the RMA was the Royal Military Academy at Woolwich

explanation.surface: An army unit covers up a mistake, if supported by a military college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land army' looks like the wartime Women's Land Army, but 'Land' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, meaning dry land as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Pageant's design

blocks.note: first meaning: a military display of marching and music, such as the Edinburgh event
second meaning: a picture inked permanently into the skin

explanation.surface: Someone admires how a pageant has been designed.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tattoo is an outdoor show of bands and drills; a tattoo is also an inked picture on skin.

clue.text: China's difficult problem: corruption

blocks.note: a teaser is a tricky puzzle
vice is moral corruption

explanation.surface: A news line about the country China and its trouble with corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' with its capital letter reads as the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is a matching set of porcelain cups, saucers and pot, so it is fine crockery.

clue.text: Incitement to disorder, first to last, in books

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

blocks.note: sedition is speech or action stirring rebellion

explanation.surface: Seditious material is found in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions are printed issues of a publication, so the word stands for books or versions of them.

clue.text: Queen taken into museum gallery

indicators.note: something taken into a place goes inside it

blocks.note: the V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch is shown round a gallery in a London museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallery' looks like part of the museum but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open platform along the outside of a house, a kind of gallery.

clue.text: Stop finding storage space for tin or bottle

indicators.note: giving something storage room means holding it within

blocks.note: to deter is to put someone off acting
a tin and a can are the same container

explanation.surface: A kitchen dilemma: where to store a tin or a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass vessel for serving wine or spirits.

clue.text: Chemical compound providing energy at crucial time

blocks.note: pep is vigour or energy
tide is an old word for a time or season, and the turn of the tide is a critical moment

explanation.surface: A supplement that gives a boost just when it is most needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A peptide is a short chain of amino acids linked together, a class of organic molecule.

clue.text: Routine established by old interviewer on Radio 4 programme

blocks.note: Sir Robin Day was a famously combative BBC political interviewer
Today is BBC Radio 4's flagship morning news show

explanation.surface: A broadcasting veteran set up the regular format of a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-to-day describes ordinary, everyday business, so it means habitual or regular.

clue.text: Let out again to be free

blocks.note: first meaning: rent out a property once more
second meaning: to set loose

explanation.surface: A prisoner is let out once more and is free.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the word as RE-LEASE, a property let a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a captive is to liberate them; to re-lease a flat is to rent it to a tenant again.

clue.text: One trying to look clever gets wicket - one at crease out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket smart alec takes a wicket and the batsman at the crease is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line a batsman stands at in cricket; 'out' reads as the dismissal but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all who pretends to wisdom, someone showing off supposed cleverness.

clue.text: One may keep close to one's neighbour in bad weather

definitions.text: One may keep close to one's neighbour in bad weather

blocks.clueFragment: One may keep close to one's neighbour in bad weather
blocks.note: surface reading: a person huddling up to the person next door during a storm

blocks.clueFragment: One may keep close to one's neighbour in bad weather
blocks.note: setter's reading: a line on a weather map, packed tightly beside the next one when a storm is coming

explanation.surface: Neighbours huddle together for comfort during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: On a weather chart these lines join points of equal pressure; when they bunch close together, winds are strong.
explanation.definitionFit: These map lines link places with the same barometric pressure, and closely spaced ones forecast gales.

clue.text: Stops keeping right?

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: stays means halts or stops
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A driver gives up keeping to the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: one who wanders off stops keeping to the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the proper course, so someone who strays no longer keeps to it.

clue.text: Light bench

blocks.note: first meaning: to alight or come to rest, as a bird does
second meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light bench' reads as a seat that weighs little, but 'Light' is the verb meaning to land.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird settles on a branch when it comes down to perch; an old-fashioned high-backed wooden seat is also called this.

clue.text: Study that is occupied by archdeacon with New Testament handy

indicators.note: a place occupied by someone has that person inside it

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
NT is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A church dignitary has a study and a Bible within easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable; that title goes between the study word and 'that is', with the scripture abbreviation after.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient is close at hand and easy to use, the same sense as handy.

clue.text: Fool may want river raked out for this

definitions.text: Fool may want river raked out for this

blocks.clueFragment: Fool may want river raked out for this
blocks.note: surface reading: an idiot wants a river dredged for some lost object

blocks.clueFragment: Fool may want river raked out for this
blocks.note: setter's reading: the Wiltshire tale of yokels raking a pond for the reflection of the night sky's disc, which made them famous as fools

explanation.surface: A simpleton wants a river dredged to recover something.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire people are nicknamed Moonrakers after a story of men raking water for a reflection; outsiders took them for fools.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflection the legendary fools tried to rake from the water was that of the earth's natural satellite.

clue.text: Congregate in American state briefly

blocks.note: first meaning: to gather together in large numbers
second meaning: the short form of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: People gather together in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To mass is to assemble in a crowd; the four-letter form is the traditional abbreviation of Massachusetts.

clue.text: Being left in Paris is awkward

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for left-hand
second meaning: socially clumsy, borrowed into English

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in the French capital feels uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being left' sounds like being abandoned, but it is the direction, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: French for left-hand has passed into English for someone clumsy or tactless, since the left hand was thought unskilled.

clue.text: Mean lass butchered agent

indicators.note: butchered means hacked about and mangled, so these letters are chopped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel girl has been murdered by an operative.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman acts for a company in selling its goods, so he is its representative or sales agent.
